problem:
Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {b}_{1}\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ be linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}].$
Given that ${\lambda }_{1}=2\text{i}$ is an eigenvalue of $A,$ find the value of $\frac{{a}_{1}{a}_{2}}{{b}_{1}{b}_{2}}.$
worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,{\lambda }_{1}=2\text{i}$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-{\lambda }_{1}I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-2\text{i} & 4 \\ -2 & -2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(2-2\text{i}){x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+(-2-2\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-2\text{i}I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as the free variable. For example, from the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}(1-\text{i}){x}_{1}
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -\frac{1}{2}(1-\text{i}){x}_{1}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=-2,$ we get the eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

 

On the other hand, since ${\lambda }_{1}=2\text{i}$ is a complex eigenvalue of $A,$ the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the  complex conjugate of ${\lambda }_{1}.$ Therefore, 

$$
{\lambda }_{2}=\overset{―}{{\lambda }_{1}}=-2\text{i}.
$$

Moreover, the corresponding eigenvector of ${\lambda }_{2}$ is

$$
{v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\frac{{a}_{1}{a}_{2}}{{b}_{1}{b}_{2}}=\frac{(-2)(-2)}{(1-\text{i})(1+\text{i})}=2.
$$
